articles.title: The New York Times is starting to test its take on Scrabble
articles.summary: The New York Times is launching a Scrabble-like game it calls Crossplay in New Zealand. It is also testing a logic game called Pips.
articles.body: The New York Times’ games team is trying something new: it’s about to start testing a Scrabble-like game it calls Crossplay, but instead of folding the game into the main NYT Games app, Crossplay will be a standalone app. The game is soft launching in New Zealand on iOS on June 10th. I was recently shown a demo of the game by Jonathan Knight, head of games at NYT, and I think it will look familiar to any fans of Scrabble or Words with Friends. The game takes place between two players. Each turn, your goal is to build a word out of the up to seven letter tiles on your tray and the letters already on the board. Every letter has a different point value, and you can boost your score by taking advantage of bonus tiles on the board that multiply your letter or word scores. The NYT has a few of its own tweaks to differentiate Crossplay from similar games, including different positions for bonus tiles and a different letter distribution, Knight says. The end of the game has a clever twist, too: after all of the letter tiles have been drawn from the virtual bag, each player gets just one additional turn instead of having to clear their tray of tiles to end the game. Knight argues that Crossplay is its own app because it’s an experience that would be hard to fit in another app. “We’re very specifically wanting to reach all new audiences with this game,” particularly people that love to compete and love word games, he says. Crossplay requires a free NYT account to play, and your friends from the main NYT Games app will carry over, Knight says. “Certain aspects” of the game will be exclusive to paid subscribers, such as a feature that will help you review your matches. But he says Crossplay won’t have many of the things that can make other free mobile games frustrating. “In a world where mobile games have become little mini casinos, and it’s often hard to find the game itself behind all of the treasure chests and friction and aggressive monetization tactics and coins and all of that, we’re really presenting a very pure, classic, elevated version of the game that you can just get in and enjoy without all that business,” Knight says. If you’re not in New Zealand, you should be able to see the App Store page for the app by copying and pasting the URL from this link into your browser. The NYT’s acquisition of Wordle arguably kicked off the race for daily puzzle games, with places like Hearst, LinkedIn, Netflix, and Zynga putting their own stamps on the genre. Overall, the NYT’s games business is growing, according to Knight, including “tremendous downloads,” growing app use, and subscriptions. NYT puzzles were played 11.1 billion times in 2024, according to statistics shared with The Verge by NYT spokesperson Jordan Cohen. Wordle was played 5.3 billion times, “3.3 billion successful Connections were made,” and Strands, the NYT’s word search game, was played 1.3 billion times. The NYT games team is still developing new puzzles for the main games app, such as Pips, a logic game, that it started beta testing in Canada in April. [Image: Pips. Update, June 10th: Added screenshots of Crossplay.

articles.title: Wordle is turning into a primetime TV game show on NBC
articles.summary: NBC has greenlit a game show version of Wordle that is set to debut in 2027. Savannah Guthrie will host.
articles.body: Wordle could be the next great game show. NBC has greenlit a game show version of The New York Times’ popular puzzle game, and it’s set to debut in 2027 with Savannah Guthrie as the host. The show will be produced by Universal Television Alternative Studio “in partnership with” Jimmy Fallon’s production company and the NYT, according to a press release. Here’s an overview of how the new “fast-paced format” will work in game show form, from the NYT: > The series will feature teams of players competing to solve five-letter word puzzles in a high-energy, collaborative environment, translating the core elements of Wordle into a new kind of viewing experience. Casting is open now for teams of three. If you want to throw your hat in the ring, you have until May 29th at 8PM ET to apply. Deadline reported last year that Fallon’s company, Electric Hot Dog, was helping with NBC’s pilot of the Wordle show.

articles.title: No, I Have Not Seen Jason’s Penis in GTA 6
articles.summary: IGN cannot confirm or deny if GTA 6 will feature full-frontal nudity, but we can confirm that we have not seen Jason's penis.
articles.body:
There are many things we at IGN expected people to take away from our big interview with Rockstar North about Grand Theft Auto 6 . The fact that I may or may not have seen protagonist Jason Duval’s penis was not particularly high on that list.

In my coverage, I mentioned a scene in which Jason is naked in the shower. This has apparently led some corners of the internet to conclude that I was treated to a full-frontal reveal of one of GTA 6’s leading men. For the sake of journalistic accuracy, I feel compelled to clarify: I did not see Jason’s penis.

Yes, Jason was naked. Yes, he was in the shower. But thanks to some carefully positioned camera angles, his modesty remained entirely intact. Whatever Rockstar has or hasn’t rendered beneath the belt remains a mystery to me, just as it does to you. Yes, that naughty leaker has been at it again , but we can't be sure when that footage was taken, which "assets" are just for the developer builds, and what will make it into the final game.

I appreciate that this may be disappointing news to those hoping for an exclusive report on the state of Jason’s anatomy, but I can only write about what I’ve actually seen. And trust me, if I had seen it, you would have gotten more than a single sentence.

Of course, if Jason does indeed have a fully-rendered penis, he won't be the first GTA character to have one. Grand Theft Auto 5 offered a semi-obscured look at Trevor's crown jewels during a custcene. Meanwhile, players who explored the mountains surrounding Los Santos will have come across the Altruist Cult, which features several fully-nude members (ahem) among its number.

The fact that nudity will be in the game had previously been confirmed by the leaked European PEGI rating for GTA 6 . "There are also strong sexual themes, including nudity, scenes of intercourse and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes," it revealed. "In various night clubs the player can also pay for private dances, during which, the game allows the player to move their hands onto the dancers’ breasts and buttocks." It stopped short of confirming full-frontal nudity, though.

IGN remains committed to bringing you the most important GTA 6 news as it happens. Apparently, this now includes genital visibility. For today's non-nude headlines, check out CBS News' astonished report about how accurately GTA 6 recreates Miami , and the Australian government's advice on how to take time off to play GTA 6 .

Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

articles.title: LEGO The Marvel Skyline Set Announced
articles.summary: LEGO has announced a new set depicting all the most recognizable buildings in the Marvel universe, including the Daily Bugle, Avengers Tower, and more.
articles.body:
With New York Comic-Con in full swing between now and October 11, LEGO has taken the opportunity to announce a new Marvel LEGO set. It’s a 1,261-piece set called The Marvel Skyline, and it's an ambitious microscale recreation of the most famous buildings in the Marvel universe, complete with a Galactus minifigure. Available to preorder now at Amazon and LEGO , it will be released January 1 for $99.99.

LEGO Marvel: The Marvel Skyline includes tiny builds of numerous buildings from the Marvel universe — more than are obvious at a glance. It has the Daily Bugle building from Spider-Man, the Avengers Tower, the Baxter Building from Fantastic 4, and Kingpin’s Fisk Tower, and a lot more besides.

In addition to the buildings, a number of creatures and vehicles are flying through the air. There’s the Avengers Quinjet, the Fantastic 4’s Excelsior ship, and the X-Men’s X-Jet. A microscale Human Torch is making a figure four in the air above the Baxter Building, and there’s even a Chitauri Leviathan swooping around. A microscale version of Spider-Man is also included.

I know some LEGO fans aren’t fond of microscale sets, but I like them. The super-small sale requires an extra level of creativity in the design, in order to make recognizable things with such a small number of tiny pieces.

The scale here is such that the Galactus minifigure looks positively huge among the buildings, which is fitting for the character. Basically, the set packs a lot of detail into a small amount of space — and a relatively small number of bricks, for what it depicts.

If you’re more of a minifigure-scale fan, LEGO released the Avengers: Doomsday New Avengers Tower ( see it at Amazon ) just a few days ago as one of the October releases . For more, check out the three recently announced LEGO Batman sets (including a legitimately terrifying Joker wall art), and take a look at our picks for the best Marvel LEGO sets available to buy right now.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Alexa Plus is better at running my home, but it’s not ready to run my life
articles.summary: Amazon’s AI-powered Alexa is more reliable and useful, but it falls short as an all-purpose assistant.
articles.body: Of all the things Alexa Plus can do, I never expected it to make me cry. Since my son left for college, the Echo Show in my office has been making then-and-now photo montages: the toddler with his first tennis racket next to the captain of his varsity team; me hugging him as a tween beside me hugging him as a young man. I’ve teared up more than once. But then comes the ad, a full-screen photo of a hideous brown leather recliner. I go from nostalgic joy to irritation in an instant. That pretty much sums up my year with Alexa Plus. One minute it will do something seriously impressive; the next, it acts like it doesn’t know who I am. [Image: Alexa Plus’s memories feature pulls images from your Alexa Photos albums. It’s become very good at pairing images from over the years, like these two of my son and me. I’ve been testing Amazon’s AI-powered Alexa Plus assistant in my home since July 2025, shortly after it launched in early access and ahead of its full launch in February 2026. With Google’s rollout of Gemini for Home earlier this year, and rumors that Apple is finally bringing the full Apple Intelligence experience to Apple Home this month, now felt like a good moment to review Amazon’s progress. A year in, Alexa Plus is the best smart home assistant I’ve tested: It’s easy to talk to, handles routines and multistep commands, and helps in the kitchen. But Amazon’s attempts to stretch it into a personal assistant are underbaked and frustrating, and the ads on the Echo Show smart displays are out of control. [Image: The Echo Dot Max is the flagship Alexa Plus speaker and your best option if you want to run Alexa without seeing ads every day. Alexa is more reliable in my smart home I tested Alexa Plus with an Echo Show 11 in my kitchen, Pops and Dots around my house, and a Show 15 and 8 in my office. I use voice commands to control my smart home devices, help me with timers and recipes, add events to my calendar and groceries to my shopping list, and occasionally order something from Amazon. I use the screen-based devices as photo frames, for viewing camera feeds, and as touchscreen controllers for my smart home. A lot has improved. Smart home control, routines, general queries, calendar management, and shopping are light-years ahead of pre-AI Alexa, mostly because the new Alexa understands me better. The big promise of LLM-powered voice assistants was the ability to say what you want without using stilted, precise nomenclature. In my testing, that’s proven out. My family uses Alexa more now than they used to, and I like being able to give more general instructions, like “Alexa, make it brighter in here” and “Alexa, I’m cold,” and it knows what to do. [Image: The Echo Show’s calendar interface is much better, though it still isn’t as good as the Skylight Calendar for viewing multiple schedules. It’s also now faster and more reliable. When I started testing the new assistant, I ran into a litany of issues, from misunderstood commands to messed-up routines and very slow responses. Today, questions about the weather or general knowledge and commands like setting a timer execute in three to five seconds, a big change from the 10 to 15 seconds I saw in 2025. When it gets a request wrong the first time, a follow-up now usually fixes it. I can say “Lock the front door, turn off the lights, turn down the thermostat, and tell the robot to clean downstairs,” and it happens promptly, without any back talk. Alexa is also much better at answering questions, especially in the kitchen. Talking with it is easier now that you can speak conversationally and don’t have to repeat the wake word — but I had to switch to the new Brief personality mode after one too many superlatives about my shopping list ( “Oooh, that will make for one spicy salsa!). [Image: The Show 8 and Show 11 are very good smart displays (ads aside). The Ring security camera integration is impressive — I can ask when I last had a package delivered, and it will show the clip and tell me what’s in the package (if it was from Amazon). I recently snapped a picture of my friend’s Dutch baby recipe while in England and sent it to Alexa via the app. When I got home, I asked Alexa to help me cook it; the assistant pulled up the reformatted recipe, and we chatted back and forth easily while I cooked. I could ask, “What temperature should I preheat the oven?” and “How many ounces are 160 grams?” and it would remember we were discussing the recipe and give the right answer. Alexa still sometimes forgets what it’s doing, and getting back to the recipe can be tricky, but it’s the best voice-assistant cooking experience I’ve tested. --- What is Alexa Plus? Alexa Plus is Amazon’s revamped digital assistant powered by generative AI. You can access it by voice through Echo smart speakers and displays, Fire TV, and other Alexa-built-in devices. You can also access it in the Alexa app on smartphones and tablets and at Alexa.com. It is free to use on the web, in the app, and on Fire TV but requires an Amazon Prime membership or a $19.99-a-month subscription (in the US) to access on compatible Echo devices. Alexa Plus is available in the U.S. and Canada and is in early access in Mexico, the U.K., Italy, Spain, Germany, Austria, France, Brazil, Australia, and India. The original Alexa is still available for free on Echo devices. --- I’ve also found Alexa more useful for general knowledge, something it used to be terrible at, and calendar management has become more reliable, too. I can now email and upload documents and photos to Alexa Plus, and it can import events from them into my calendar. I added my daughter’s entire school schedule that way. Shopping is also hugely improved. I uploaded 10 screenshots of sewing supplies from my daughter’s teacher to the Alexa app, and it found all the items and added them to my Amazon cart, saving me a lot of time. My favorite upgrade is creating Alexa smart home routines by voice. I think of something I want my home to do, tell Alexa, and it does it. I wanted the string lights on the porch to turn on when I walk outside; Alexa set up a routine using the motion sensor on the Ring camera. I can also adapt routines on the fly. One night, my daughter came out of her bathroom complaining, “The lights kept shutting off.” I told Alexa to change the “Hallway bathroom light” routine to shut off after 30 minutes instead of 15, and it fixed it. But it took a long time to get here. Like many Alexa users, I had a lot of technical debt in my smart home, and as a reviewer, my Alexa app was a graveyard of zombie devices. To get Alexa Plus to work properly for me, I had to rebuild my smart home from scratch, deleting all my old Alexa skills and routines and killing dead and duplicate devices. It took months, literally. I’ve had to re-add 55 Hue devices six times over the past year. And while Alexa has improved, the Alexa app has not. Adding, deleting, and moving multiple devices is still deeply painful, and the app experience is Alexa’s biggest flaw. What I really want is Alexa Plus to manage all that for me so I never have to touch the app. From setting up gadgets to troubleshooting issues, Alexa should be able to put devices in the right room and, if something isn’t working, figure it out. I want it to manage my smart home for me. That is an assistant I would pay money for. [Image: The ads on the Echo Show smart displays are Alexa Plus’s worst feature. Agents, accuracy, and ads While Alexa Plus has made a lot of improvements, there are three big issues, one of which may make you flat-out not want to use the service: ads, inconsistency, and mostly failed attempts at being a personal assistant. Display ads are out of control. Every Show device is now a rotating billboard in my home for Amazon goods. Even if you turn off all the homescreen content (the rotating screen on the displays), you still get ads interspersed between your photos and the clock. Timing is random; I can see one an hour on the Echo Show 5 in the bedroom and then go a whole day without seeing one on the 11 in my kitchen, but they’re fairly constant on the Show 8 in my office. Daniel Rausch, VP of Alexa & Echo at Amazon, tells me these ads are curated and designed to be relevant. “When it’s done well, an ad should show up with something useful at just the right moment,” he said. But it hasn’t felt curated to me; among the beauty products, car accessories, snacks, furniture, health supplements, and smart home gear that have assaulted my eyeballs, nothing has been something I wanted to buy. Even worse, Amazon recently added video ads. There is now a fix, but it will cost you: Amazon’s new Photo Gallery Unlimited feature removes the ads from the homescreen for $2.99 per month per device. If you don’t want to pay monthly to avoid ads, I would stick with the Echo speakers. [Image: Amazon trying to sell my 15-year-old daughter motor oil doesn’t feel “curated.” Though the anti-aging cream ad I saw one morning did hurt. Alexa Plus is still inconsistent at executing more complicated requests. This was a big issue in my initial testing and has improved, but not gone away. The shift from the reliable but restricted command-and-control architecture of the old Alexa to the LLM-powered generative AI has introduced a lot of uncertainty: Alexa Plus sometimes has to guess at what you want. [Image: Alexa Plus misheard my request for a Coffee Grande and instead generated an image of a coffee grinder. For example, Alexa still can’t reliably make a cup of coffee. I have an Alexa-capable Bosch 800 Series coffee machine with a special integration that gives Alexa more granular controls, including making a specific drink, such as a coffee grande. This works most of the time — a big improvement over my initial testing. But the other day I asked Alexa to make me a coffee grande, and it replied, “I’d love to, but I’m fresh out of arms and a coffee maker.” I asked again, and it said, “Sure, here’s a coffee grinder,” displaying an AI-generated image of a coffee grinder. Alexa Plus still struggles with timely information. Asking it when England next played in the soccer World Cup in June almost made me miss kickoff, and last month when I asked what channel an Ohio State–Illinois football game was on, it offered to set up a reminder for a game that had already started. Getting dates and times wrong is not a trait I want in a personal assistant, which is what Amazon is pushing Alexa Plus as. Instead of a stoic, disembodied voice, I’m now greeted every morning by a perky pair of digital hands proffering a cheery emoji and a line like “Hey Jen, tell me what I can do for you today?” on the Echo Show in my kitchen. Perkiness aside — I’m English; we don’t do perky — I’m not against Alexa doing more for me. It’s just that the assistant has failed to finish several tasks I’ve given it. Most of these new agentic features, including integrations with Thumbtack, OpenTable, and Ticketmaster, feel underbaked and mostly a waste of my time. This feature-stuffing is inevitable as Amazon starts charging to use Alexa on Echo devices ($19.99 a month if you aren’t a Prime member) and competes with the AI giants in the agentic space. But nothing is more frustrating than spending time explaining what you want done, only to then have to do it yourself. [Image: Trying to order lunch with Uber Eats using voice and touch on the Show 8 was frustrating and ultimately unsuccessful. When I tried ordering lunch through Uber Eats on the Echo Show, Alexa confidently told me, “Just tell me what you like, and I’ll find it on the menu as you speak.” That wasn’t the case. Instead, I spent 20 minutes trying to order a Chick-fil-A meal with iced tea, while the Uber Eats interface on the smart display insisted on ordering me a s’mores milkshake I never asked for. Booking an electrician was no better; after 10 minutes dictating my electrical issues to Alexa and going through several Thumbtack sign-up screens, it gave me the electrician’s number to call. A bigger problem is memory. Alexa has the memory of a goldfish. For a while, it forgot who I was and kept asking me to introduce myself whenever I asked it to do something. Which was frankly rude, since it’s been living in my house for a decade. It’s also supposed to have a feature called Remember This that stores information you tell it, similar to the memory features in ChatGPT or Claude. I told it what school my daughter went to, asked it to remember this, then asked what the traffic was like getting there. It gave the correct answer. But the next day, when I made the same request, it confidently gave me the traffic conditions and travel time to an entirely different school, and it insisted that was the school I’d asked it to remember. Remembering details about you, your household, and your home is a crucial skill for a personal assistant. If I hired one that sent my daughter to the wrong school, I’d fire them immediately. [Image: Alexa Plus has deeper integration with this smart Bosch coffee machine, making it better at handling more granular commands — such as “Make me a coffee grande” — but it’s inconsistent. Amazon already knows a lot about my household, from what I buy to what’s on my shopping list and even what arrives at my front door — that’s a privacy tradeoff you have to grapple with when using Alexa. What it lacks is the personal context a personal assistant needs. This is where Google and Apple have the lead, and where Amazon has a lot of catching up to do to succeed here. I test all the major smart home assistants, including Google’s Gemini for Home and Siri in Apple Home, and Alexa is the most reliable and functional for controlling my home. But I’ll turn to Siri to send a text message or Google to get me a traffic-free route to my daughter’s school. With Alexa Plus, Amazon has taken a big step toward the ambient smart home the company has imagined for over a decade. What it needs to do now is avoid the temptation to become a general-purpose AI bot, and instead focus on becoming the brain for your home — potentially one you could integrate with your personal AI assistant of choice (something Google is doing with Google Home). This would require Amazon to rediscover the openness that defined the platform when it launched in 2014 — it increasingly feels closed, with features that work only with Amazon’s brands and curated partners. But Alexa remains the biggest mainstream smart home platform, with broad third-party support, a huge install base, and wide support for protocols — including Matter and Thread. Where it wins in breadth, however, Alexa lacks in depth. Alexa Plus should be able to control every feature of every device, not just on and off (Amazon recently launched a developer toolkit that could help here). Combined with its Omnisense fusion sensor platform, announced last year, this could bring it much closer to fully learning and understanding your household’s patterns. With that context, it could suggest proactive routines and start taking action for you — beyond random hunches every now and then. That’s the next frontier for the smart home, and today Amazon is best poised to overcome it. The smart home assistant I want isn’t the one that can book a restaurant or write an email; it’s the one that understands my home, can manage it for me, and knows when I need a cute baby pic to cheer me up. Photos by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

articles.title: ‘It’s Almost Not Worth Being Number Two’ – How Live-Service Turned Games Into a Battle Royale for the Top Spot
articles.summary: The live-service trend has brought us some amazing games, but the chase for money-printing success means developers have become trapped in a bloody battle royale that's stifling creativity.
articles.body:
Before there was Warzone, Fortnite, or even PUBG: Battlegrounds, there was Minecraft Survival Games. While the exact origin is nebulous, Norwegian YouTuber Dennis Vaeride is credited as launching the first Survival Games server in April 2012, just one month after The Hunger Games’ film adaptation had opened in cinemas. The concept followed the rules outlined in Katniss’ harrowing ordeal: dozens of players would sprint into the middle of a starting circle, gather supplies, and then hunt until the last one standing.

Little did Vaeride know, he’d just fired the starting pistol on an industry-wide battle royale. Many studios would try to replicate this formula. Few would survive. Those that did would grow fat on microtransactions and spiralling player counts.

Last year the market for the battle royale sub-genre was valued at $11.2 billion. It is expected to reach nearly $30 billion by 2035 . Everyone’s chasing the money and almost all of them are discovering just how difficult it is to carve out their own piece of the pie – even heavyweights like Halo Studios and monied companies like Amazon Games have failed miserably. It’s a financial frenzy that can be traced all the way back to those Hunger Games-inspired Minecraft servers… although the true spark that set the industry ablaze came a year later, from a single developer living in Brazil.

In early 2013, Brendan Greene had an idea for a DayZ mod (the zombie survival game that was itself a mod of mil-sim ARMA, and was already responsible for whipping the survival genre into a frenzy on PC). Inspired not by The Hunger Games but by Kinji Fukasaku’s similarly themed 2000 thriller, Battle Royale, Greene’s idea was a last-player-standing multiplayer mode that took place on a large map scattered with weapons and restricted by a shrinking circular safe area. He developed what became PlayerUnknown's Battle Royale over a number of years, and his association with the format became so significant that Sony brought him on as a consultant whilst developing the competing H1Z1.

But Sony wasn’t the only major studio that took notice of Greene’s rise. South Korean studio Bluehole offered him the chance to create his own project. That game was PlayerUnknown Battlegrounds – a 100-player last-man-standing shooter with random loot drops and an ever-decreasing map size. The game launched on Steam Early Access in March 2017. By December, it had over three million concurrent players. Everyone took notice of Greene’s success – including Epic Games.

Fortnite was not always the battle royale you know today. When it launched in July 2017, it was a struggling tower defence game where a quartet of players scavenged and built fortifications to defend against waves of nocturnal monsters. PUBG’s meteoric success convinced Epic’s CEO and CCO, Tim Sweeney and Donald Mustard, to take a gamble on improving Fortnite’s future: they quickly tasked the team to develop their own equivalent of PlayerUnknown’s formula.

By September, the mode was released. It was barebones, practically ramshackle, with minimal assets and a bizarre application of the building systems from the original fort-crafting mode. But it had one secret weapon. Unlike PUBG, Fortnite: Battle Royale was free-to-play. The most popular video game idea in the world was suddenly free for all. Within 2 weeks, it hit 10 million players. Within a year, it was home to 125 million. Today, the number of registered Fortnite players sits at 650 million.

The battle royale pivot changed Fortnite forever. It isn’t even a game anymore – it’s become a platform, one where Ariana Grande and Eminem have performed virtually, previews of Star Wars movies have played, and servers worldwide were shut down to emulate a world-ending event.

It’s Happened Before, It Will Happen Again

PUBG and Fortnite’s dual success created a video games arms race: nearly 2,000 games have been assigned the “battle royale” tag on Steam, while hundreds more exist in the mobile gaming market. When you have a game that made $9 billion within two years and likely over $20 billion by now, it’s clear to see why so many publishers have tried to replicate its formula.

This is, of course, an echo of one of the original live-service booms from half a decade earlier: the MOBA. Another genre that grew out of a mod, the industry was captivated by the 5v5 “battle arena”, with dozens of studios attempting to replicate the success of Riot’s League of Legends and Valve’s Dota 2 . Dozens of MOBAs were quickly developed and died almost as fast, and the same cycle could be seen with battle royale. Ubisoft’s Hyper Scape , Square Enix’s Final Fantasy 7: The First Soldier , Fallout 76’s Nuclear Winter expansion – even Epic itself couldn’t emulate its own success, with wrestling battle royale Rumbleverse flatlining less than a year after launch.

Some may claim the widespread failure to truly compete with PUBG and Fortnite is down to studios failing to innovate on Greene’s original concepts. But, as with the MOBA craze, a massively over-saturated marketplace may be the stronger prevailing reason. It’s a situation ex-BioWare producer Mark Darrah, who worked on looter shooter Anthem , knows well.

“You have to believe that you can actually dethrone one of the top two players in that genre, or you shouldn’t be doing it,” he says. For Darrah, that meant stealing the crown from Destiny – a task that the single-player RPG experts at BioWare weren’t suited to. Anthem struggled right from the moment it launched. Destiny remained on the throne.

But there’s more to that story. BioWare wasn’t just competing with Destiny – it was going up against a Destiny that had enjoyed half a decade of development, refinement, and a sequel. That’s an issue facing any developer getting into the live-service space in 2026 – the table stakes for new video games are radically different to even just 10 years ago. As Overwatch’s original lead director Jeff Kaplan puts it: “If someone wanted to make a MOBA today, they’re not competing with the likes of League of Legends five years in. They’re competing with League up to today.”

The Poisoned Chalice of Live-Service Success

Overwatch , the live-service game that triggered the hero shooter craze, was not planned. Kaplan was given an ultimatum after his previous MMORPG project fell apart: give us an idea within a month or the team gets disbanded.

Kaplan feels that pressure created an intense creativity boost amongst the team, both during the initial concepting and development of the 6v6 hero shooter, and beyond into its live years. The game “caught and rode the [audience] wave”, describes Kaplan, who compares it to World of Warcraft’s similar success.

“[The launch and first year’s success] was all because of improvisation, of just knowing and feeling what felt cool in the moment,” Kaplan explains.

Seven million people played Overwatch in its first week, entranced by its smart melding of heroes and abilities with FPS arena action. This wasn’t another contender to the fading MOBA trend, but something fresh and new and worth spending hundreds of hours with. Within five months, that number ballooned to 20 million. By the end of Overwatch’s first year, 30 million players were High Nooning and Dragonstriking one another across the hero shooter’s maps. Kaplan attributes his team’s success to their fluidity when it came to devising the game’s future, describing their development style as akin to an improvisational jazz band. A successful launch is the peak for a single-player game, but for live-service it’s just the beginning. Keeping Overwatch in peak condition was the key to ensuring it remained the live service shooter to play – something Blizzard achieved… until it didn’t.

Overwatch’s success created a loop: the development team would expand to make new and interesting updates, making the game more expensive to run, giving upper management an in-road to question the core fundamentals of that success, and how profit margins can be not only rebalanced, but perhaps outsized.

“People would say, ‘League of Legends is free-to-play, look at that. Why don’t you switch Overwatch? We could do it next month.’” recalls Kaplan. “It’s that one-size-fits-all mentality that is poison for development teams.”

And here we reach what many would perceive as both the promise and the problem at the heart of live-service games: there’s always more money to be made. This format isn’t about selling copies at launch, it's about continual profit, day after day, month after month, year after year. Kaplan eventually left Blizzard in 2021 following his disagreement with executive plans – management wanted to aggressively monetize his vision of Overwatch 2 in order to fund the game’s external esports league. Clashing viewpoints meant Blizzard lost Kaplan. When something becomes a monster success, it seems that those who own the monster may be willing to sacrifice the people who tamed it in the first place, if the price is right.

“They didn’t let the team really focus on what they wanted to focus on,” Kaplan remembers. He notes that the Overwatch 2 that eventually released was very different to his own sequel concept, although he praises the team for their efforts in continuing the franchise.

During the hero shooter explosion of the mid-2010s, many studios tried to create their own Overwatch. Ubisoft’s Rainbow Six Siege , launched a year before Blizzard’s behemoth, successfully kept its head above water, largely thanks to its unique niche of lethal action and destructible environments. But those who tried to ape Overwatch’s stylish characters and snappy arcade action were doomed to wither in its shadow. Amazon Games’ Crucible , EA’s Rocket Arena , Boss Key’s LawBreakers , and First Watch’s Rogue Company are all examples of hero shooters that have come and gone. None of them stuck for one defining reason: lack of innovation.

“Number one [in sales/player count] controls so much of the attention in a space that it’s almost not worth being number two, let alone five or six”, says Darrah. The PvP hero shooter mold has hardly been touched since Overwatch defined it. Instead, publishers have provided the illusion of innovation through marketing. “Oftentime the marketing spend for a triple-A game can dwarf the development cost”, Kaplan notes.

The high-profile case of Sony and Firewalk Studios’ 2024 hero shooter Concord was an unfortunate trifecta of these issues: despite a $400 million budget, it lacked innovation, and its attempts to promote itself through inclusion in Amazon’s Secret Level TV series weeks ahead of launch felt premature and overly-confident. But above all else, it came far too late. Concord began development in 2016, the same year Overwatch released. Had it released in 2019, or even 2020, perhaps it may have found its audience. But eight years on, you’re not competing with the Overwatch of 2016, you’re competing with Overwatch bolstered by almost a decade of development. On top of that, you’re also facing all the bodies on the road that tried to follow it… and the fact that the world has largely moved on from hero shooters, onto battle royale, and is hungry for the next big live shooter trend.

The fates of Anthem and Concord are a bleak reflection of the growing do or die mentality many publishers have begun to operate with when faced with the challenge of their assumed heavy-hitter opening to a softer-than-expected launch. We’ve already noted how BioWare was naturally going to struggle going toe-to-toe with Destiny, considering Bungie’s spiritual successor to the MMORPG had made over $325 million in five days back in 2014, becoming the biggest new franchise launch of all time. But, like Concord, Anthem suffered a protracted development that contributed to its poor chances: When it was released in 2019, many decried Anthem for ripping Destiny off. In actuality, it began life way back in 2012, before Destiny had been revealed to the world.

Darrah remembers the corporate shift that lit the fuse on Anthem’s downfall, which began shortly after EA’s success with FIFA Ultimate Team. “They wanted every franchise to be a billion-dollar franchise”, he said, recalling internal goals for every franchise to hit minimum 40% profit margins, and making minimum $50 million in profit. BioWare was very much not primed to achieve such financial results – even its beloved Mass Effect series was not the kind of dollar-raking blockbuster that EA demanded. The studio’s approach had to change to appease its masters. BioWare had to go live-service.

Darrah remembers the way Anthem was sold to EA: “What if we said it’s still BioWare, but it’s completely not BioWare?” That confusing elevator pitch was the start of what would be a painful journey for BioWare’s RPG artists. Anthem was pitched internally as ‘the future of storytelling’ by director Casey Hudeon, but no one at BioWare, including Darrah, understood what that meant, even as the project approached its launch.

While the very people making Anthem were concerned about its heading, Darrah believes EA’s interest in the project aligned with the same reasons why the publisher’s favourite BioWare game was its second set in Thedas: “[Dragon Age 2] wasn’t well received, didn’t sell as well as other BioWare games – but it was the balance of math in terms of finances that made their line go up,” he says. Anthem, with its live-service design, presented the opportunity for BioWare to push a line up.

Darrah wasn’t one of the original Anthem developers, but in October 2017 he was moved from working on Dragon Age: The Veilguard to shepherd (and essentially save) Anthem’s development. Many credit his leadership as the reason why Anthem even made it out of the door. It launched in February 2019 to poor review scores and significant technical issues, an unsurprising result given the game was essentially redeveloped within a year.

And yet Anthem became BioWare’s second fastest-selling game behind Mass Effect 3, earning over $100 million in digital revenue in the first month. As a pure product of commerce, Anthem ticked all of EA’s boxes. But live-service is not about those initial sales – it’s about the marathon that lies beyond. And while attempts were made to improve Anthem, its sub-standard design failed to hold player interest long enough to allow the improvements to flourish. All development ceased in 2021. As of this year, it’s totally unplayable.

While both Concord and Anthem would find themselves victims of a similar fate, the journey to that fate differs significantly. Anthem was afforded six years to find an audience. Concord was given less than two weeks. If Concord had released in 2019, perhaps it may have eventually found its footing and carved out its own niche, similar to Hello Games’ own journey with No Man’s Sky. But if Anthem had been released in 2024, can anyone imagine it truly lasting longer than Concord did?

In an ironic twist of fate, Anthem’s initial success only caused more friction between BioWare and EA. Dragon Age: The Veilguard’s development was directly impacted. Its initial concept contained live-service elements based on Anthem’s code per EA’s direction, only for it all to change course following Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order’s success as a single-player only game and Anthem’s ultimately short lifespan. Similar to Anthem, The Veilguard’s final shape was a confusing abstraction, a BioWare game in appearance only, lacking the studio’s key pillars of narrative depth and player choice. EA CEO Andrew Wilson’s comments that Veilguard may have fared better if it had stuck to the original live-service plans consequently not only feels like a kick in the teeth to BioWare, but casts a spotlight on the publisher’s fundamental misunderstanding of what creates the value of its franchises.

“Dragon Age has great games you can get 30, 40 hours from,” observes Kaplan. “But if you try to stretch an experience like that out to 100 hours or 1,000 hours, that game wasn’t designed to do that.”.

The battle scars worn by Anthem and Veilguard’s staff are reflective of an increasingly pervasive trend of major publishers assigning prestige single-player developers like BioWare or Rocksteady to replicate the profits of live-service studios.

“The realization that this type of game was a lottery ticket that could pay off really big shifted our industry around so much”, Darrah muses. That shift, of course, has often been in the form of mass restructuring and layoffs following an attempt to compete in the live-service arena.

It’s clear that live-service is perhaps the biggest challenge that video games have faced in a long time. Demanding huge amounts of development on never-ending timelines, they understandably encourage copycat designs as publishers attempt to create their money-printing machines. But, as we’ve seen in the format’s popularity cycles, it’s the early innovators that tend to reign… and the throne only allows for a temporary tenancy. The age of the MMO, MOBA, and hero shooter have all come and gone, and soon the sun will set on the battle royale. One of gaming market research company NewZoo’s latest reports showed a 27% decline in the battle royale sub-genre, with Fortnite and Apex Legends both suffering nearly a quarter drop in playtime growth themselves.

However, while battle royale may be the ultimate showcase for just how big live-service can be, its waning popularity is no indication of the end of live-service. We’ve been playing microtransaction-funded multiplayer games since the ‘90s, and while there are reports that free-to-play is facing decline, the revenue stream shows no sign of going away any time soon. PlayStation CEO Hidaeki Nishino’s recent recommitment to to live-service shows that even a disaster like Concord can’t deter the famously prestige single-player platform from forcing its way to success in the field. Meanwhile, Ubisoft has claimed the single-player model is outdated and EA’s Andrew Wilson proclaimed the future of single-player is live-service , all attitudes worthy of significant concern.

“I don’t think anyone wants to live in a world where there are only seven games - but that’s kind of where we’re headed if we keep pushing down this road”, Darrah laments.

Live-service isn’t an inherently bad thing. But, as with so many issues in the industry, there’s a friction between the people who make games and the people who profit from them.

“I always talk about games in terms of a pyramid,” says Kaplan. “They’re art, then entertainment, then business. If something’s not entertaining, there’s no business there. It fails. You can’t invert the pyramid.”

Like Ultima Online, EverQuest and World of Warcraft, Destiny, Fortnite and Overwatch became the three pioneering pillars of what modern live-service games could be, following Kaplan’s pyramid of creativity. It’s difficult to argue against those games offering high-quality levels of innovation, be that Destiny’s unrivaled gunplay and phenomenal raid design, Overwatch’s exceptional hero interplay, or Fortnite’s unrivalled ability to reinvent itself on a seemingly monthly basis.

But that pyramid has so often been inverted, with many chasing the money-printing success of these three titles while failing to learn from many of the valuable lessons the trio all had to overcome to ensure their success. And with so many of the industry’s major players chasing the same trends in broadly similar ways, it feels like the sky is falling all around us.

The pyramid has become inverted. And so the big question is: can it be realigned before it's too late?

Sab Astley is a freelance writer who has written for IGN, Polygon, TotalFilm, Rolling Stone, Radio Times, and Metro UK.

articles.title: GTA 6 Reveals a Handful of Radio Stations, DJs, and Songs Ahead of Release
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has launched a new website which allows you to listen to some of the radio stations and songs that will be featured in GTA 6.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games has launched a new website which allows you to listen to some of the radio stations and songs that will be featured in GTA 6 .

Rockstar said GTA 6 will feature the "biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet," and, as always, has hired a number of celebrities such as Morgan Wallen and Lana Del Rey to host the stations. As for some of the things you'll be able to listen to, here are all of the stations and some of the songs that Rockstar has revealed so far.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

Every Confirmed Radio Station in GTA 6 So Far

Cocoteo FM: Leonida's home for the best of modern Latin music. Hosted by El Martillo (voiced by Bad Bunny) and La Gata (voiced by RaiNao) and featuring everything from bachata and merengue to dembow and reggaeton – Cocoteo FM is el party que nunca se apaga .

Axel Rulay ft. Farruko & El Alfa - Si Es Trucho Es Trucho (Remix)

Romeo Santos & El Chaval de la Bachata - Canalla

Back Country Radio: MW (voiced by Morgan Wallen) and Delta Dawne (voiced by Lana Del Rey) blast renegade country music to the Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, and beyond. Stay tuned for Back Country’s roving reporter, swamp meteorologist, and Delta’s not-so-secret lover Mud Dog Mike (voiced by Jeremy Dufrene) checking in from the driver’s seat of his Grassrivers airboat.

David Allan Coe - Need a Little Time Off for Bad Behavior

Loretta Lynn - Don't Come Home A-Drinkin' (With Lovin' On Your Mind)

Hank Williams, Jr. & Waylon Jennings - The Conversation

AfroBank FM: Turn up the gbedu with Burna (voiced by Burna Boy) and Palmsy (voiced by Palms Trax), AfroBank FM's dynamic duo curating the best in African music, from 20th-century classics and undiscovered gems to contemporary sounds like amapiano, 3-step, and more.

DJ Lag & Robot Boii ft. Kamo Mphela - Shay'sana

The Chamber 106.6: Crushing metal has landed in Leonida. Jump in the pit with DJ Kerry (voiced by Kerry King) and DJ Tom (voiced by Tom Araya) for classic metal from the ‘80s and beyond as they channel Leonida’s deep metal roots.

Flash FM: The Vice City institution that delivers the best in pop music with Robyn (voiced by herself) and Alex (voiced by Alex Consani) — guaranteed to make you dance no matter where you find yourself in the Goodtime State.

Zara Larsson & PinkPantheress - Midnight Sun (Girls Trip)

Dirty South Classics: A little southern hospitality from Trick (voiced by Trick Daddy) and Trina (voiced by herself), blasting regional rap and hip-hop classics. From the beach to the block, nobody reps Leonida and the South like they do.

David Banner ft. Lil' Flip - Like A Pimp

DJ Khaled ft. Trick Daddy, Rick Ross & Pitbull - Born N Raised

This small selection does confirm there will be a wide variety of music, as some of the music featured includes the likes of Charli XCX, Bad Bunny, MGMT, DJ Khaled, and Black Sabbath. It's unclear if Rockstar will reveal the entire list of tracks in GTA 6 before launch, but this does provide a pretty good idea of what we'll be getting on November 19.

Additionally, Rockstar released a small batch of new screenshots and confirmed that GTA 6 will feature the ability to listen to on-demand podcasts and radio stations on foot by using a pair of headphones and your smartphone. This is a massive feature that fans have wanted for years, as the radio has previously been confined to your vehicles and inside of select buildings. However, now players will be able to listen to music freely when they're in combat, exploring on foot, and more.

In September, Rockstar Games confirmed that it will release an album comprised of original music, made for GTA 6. So far, Rockstar has confirmed original songs from Travis Scott, Morgan Wallen, Keith Richards, and more. The entire tracklist has yet to be revealed, but it wouldn't be surprising if we hear more about the album later this month or early November ahead of the game's launch.

All of this news is coming just hours after 25 minutes of new GTA 6 gameplay leaked on the internet . The new footage comes from Cyberleek, who was responsible for leaking a ton of GTA gameplay in August. Rockstar has yet to respond to the new footage, but is likely hoping that the news around the game's radio station serves as an ample distraction.

IGN also posted a full transcript of its interview with Rob Nelson, the studio co-head of Rockstar North . Nelson demoed GTA 6 for IGN earlier this summer and revealed a variety of new information regarding the game in our conversation with him.

GTA 6 will release on November 19 for Xbox Series X|S and PS5.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: GTA VI will have in-game podcasts and at least six radio stations
articles.summary: Rockstar announced the first six radio stations in GTA 6, which will also include in-game podcasts for the first time.
articles.body: Music is always a major part of a Grand Theft Auto game, and Rockstar Games says GTA VI will have the series’ “biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet.” There will be at least six radio stations players can listen to in vehicles or on foot, ranging from talk radio to classic rock: Cocoteo FM, Back Country Radio, AfroBank FM, The Chamber 106.6, Flash FM, and Dirty South Classics. You can sample the stations on Rockstar’s website, along with six singles from GTA VI’s official soundtrack, announced earlier this month, featuring artists like Yung Lean and Travis Scott. But there’s more to listen to than music. Rockstar also says “for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts.” So, players will be able to listen to fictional podcasters give fictional takes on fictional events while driving their fictional cars around Leonida (fictional Florida). It’s another signal of the level of realism Rockstar seems to be aiming for — Netflix’s extended preview of GTA VI also shows details like a mechanic for holding hands and police NPCs who remember what you look like. Meanwhile, a recent leak revealed much more, uh, personal details for the two main characters. Grand Theft Auto VI is available for preorder now and launches November 19th.

articles.title: Mattel Reveals an Epic DC Premium Batman Figure Based on the Iconic Hush Comic | NYCC 2026
articles.summary: With Mattel regaining the rights to DC's vast lineup of characters, we can reveal the very first DC Premium figure ahead of its debut at NYCC. And yes, it's Batman.
articles.body:
The collectibles world is undergoing a seismic shift right now. The license for DC figures is shifting from McFarlane Toys to Mattel. And while Mattel has already released a number of new kid-focused figures under the "DC Core" branding, older collectors are eagerly awaiting news about the "DC Premium" line. Just ahead of its official debut at NYCC, IGN can exclusively reveal the very first DC Premium figure. And yes, it's Batman.

Head down to the slideshow gallery below for an exclusive first look at the DC Premium Batman: Hush Rooftop Bat-Signal Diorama Set:

DC Premium Batman: Hush Rooftop Bat-Signal Diorama Set - Image Gallery

It's hardly surprising that Mattel would choose Batman of all characters to kick off the DC Premium line. This particular figure is based on the 2002-03 storyline Batman: Hush and the artwork of Jim Lee. It measures 6.5 inches tall and features no fewer than 34 points of articulation, so you should be able to get some very dynamic superhero poses out of it.

This isn't a standard action figure release, however. It's a larger bundle that includes a rooftop diorama base and a light-up Bat-Signal accessory. The display base even has the ability to create a mist effect when water is placed in the water tower. The figure also includes a posable, wired fabric cape and interchangeable hands.

“We are incredibly proud to bring DC back to Mattel, marking an exciting new chapter with the debut of Batman: Hush," said Nick Karamanos, General Manager & Head of Entertainment Partnerships, Action Figures and Preschool Entertainment at Mattel, in a statement. "We know there has been tremendous anticipation for this launch, and we’re excited to deliver what fans expect from a Mattel action figure — the very best.”

The DC Premium Batman: Hush Rooftop Bat-Signal Diorama Set is priced at $100 and is available to order now on the Mattel Creations website .

This new set will be on display at DC's NYCC booth (#4365) this week. Mattel is also teasing that future DC Premium figures will be revealed during a livestream event happening on January 1, 2027.

articles.title: Tekken 8’s Reina Teased as the Next Guest Character for Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves
articles.summary: Reina, who made her debut in Tekken 8, is coming to Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves. The announcement comes from a short teaser trailer from SNK Official.
articles.body:
Reina, who made her debut in Tekken 8 , is coming to Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves . The announcement comes from a short teaser trailer from SNK Official.

The Tekken fighter joins the City of the Wolves roster as a playable character, joining other guest characters such as Street Fighter’s Chun-Li, Fist of the North Star’s Kenshiro, and soccer star Christiano Ronaldo. Reina is believed to be the daughter of Heihachi Mishima, a guy with a penchant for chucking his kids into volcanos. It’s no wonder she’s looking for somewhere else to live.

Tekken 7 previously featured Geese Howard, one of the primary antagonists of Fatal Fury, as a guest character, so it’s nice to see Bandai Namco paying the favor back. Fatal Fury has gone a bit ham with the guest characters, but this one definitely makes more sense than that soccer player who dives for a living.

The trailer doesn’t give much away, but it’ll be interesting to see how Reina’s Mishima School fighting style gets translated into Fatal Fury. This announcement nips the heels of the Manjiro Sano and Ken Ryuguji (Season Pass 3 – fourth DLC character) trailers, also released today. Both Sano and Ryuguji, who originate from manga series Tokyo Revengers, arrive in South Town on October 22.

Reina is expected to hit City of the Wolves in December, after Laocorn is released in November. Reina also continues City of the Wolves' guest DLC character run after Sano's announcement sparked a debate in the Fatal Fury community about guest fighters .

IGN’s Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves review called it “a wonderful update to the classic SNK style of one-on-one combat that feels similar to Street Fighter 6, but just different enough to exist as an alternative to it.”

Eagle-eyed players had already predicted the inclusion of Reina, noting the purple color of Season 3 fitted with the character’s aesthetic. In the teaser trailer, she appears only as a silhouette in the background.

Reina is considered a hard character to master in Tekken 8, thanks to her diverse moveset and her weak lows. Advanced players make up for it by utilizing her unbreakable throws and stance changes.

The character’s pick rate in Tekken 8 Ranked is 3.1% and she has a 46% win rate. It remains to be seen whether she’s as deep and divisive in City of the Wolves.

articles.title: Star Wars Legend Timothy Zahn Makes the Lightspeed Jump to Star Trek in 2027 - NYCC 2026
articles.summary: In a major pop culture twist, Star Wars legend Timothy Zahn is making the jump to the Star Trek franchise to pen an original graphic novel called Star Trek: Roc's Egg.
articles.body:
Timothy Zahn is undoubtedly one of the most important names in the world of Star Wars novels. Zahn's original Thrawn trilogy of books helped birth the Expanded Universe in the early '90s , and he's continued to chart the character's course even in Disney's new Star Wars timeline. That's why it's a little surreal to learn that Zahn is now crossing that pop culture divide and making his way to the Star Trek franchise.

IDW Publishing revealed at NYCC that Zahn is penning a new graphic novel called Star Trek: Roc's Egg. The book is illustrated by Star Trek veteran Ángel Hernández.

This new graphic novel takes place on the iconic Deep Space 9 station, as the Federation launches an investigation into the destruction of a valuable artifact and uncovers a larger conspiracy. Here's the official summary for the book:

When a mysterious artifact known as a Roc’s Egg arrives on the station—and is seemingly destroyed in transit—a Federation JAG investigation is called in to uncover what really happened. But the deeper the team digs, the stranger the mystery becomes: a secret auction, a station full of wealthy collectors and dangerous criminals, a priceless artifact that may not be what it seems, and a murder waiting to happen.

From acclaimed author Timothy Zahn and artist Ángel Hernández comes Star Trek: Roc’s Egg, a twisty new mystery set aboard Deep Space 9 where everyone has something to hide—and the truth may be more valuable than the treasure itself.

“My association with Star Trek goes all the way back to 1966 and the original TV series. Now, after sixty years, I’ve been given the chance to add my own small grace note to that rich and vibrant symphony,” said Zahn in a statement. “This is a huge honor and privilege, and one which I will always cherish.”

Star Trek: Roc's Egg will be released in October 2027.

articles.title: 35% of Marvel's Wolverine Sales Were on Disc, According to Analyst Data
articles.summary: According to retail data, 35% of Marvel’s Wolverine sales were physical discs.
articles.body:
According to retail data, 35% of Marvel’s Wolverine sales were physical discs. This comes from Ampere Analysis (via The Game Business ), which tracks sales data across major markets globally.

The data suggests Wolverine shifted 2.16 million units in September (it went on sale September 15), and a significant portion of those sales were on-disc. In Europe, 51% of Wolverine sales came from the boxed version. Zooming in, more than two thirds were physical sales in France, but two thirds were digital in the UK.

The data comes in the wake of Sony's controversial announcement that it will phase out physical disc production for PlayStation by 2028, which sparked an online backlash and calls for a U-turn from some organizations who campaign for physical media.

Marvel's Wolverine: Every Costume in the PS5 Game

“If platform owners are deciding to eliminate physical media and older digital storefronts, then we'd also like to see trade groups like the Entertainment Software Association offer meaningful solutions for archives and museums to legally preserve digital-only content and make it accessible for research,” the Video Game History Foundation has said.

Earlier this month, former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden questioned Sony's decision to kill discs , saying: "I do think, particularly in the gaming realm, maybe 80% of the people download and 20% don't, whatever that breakdown might be, but that's a super important 20%. I mean, that is largely the most faithful of the faithful, that is, many times, the people who buy two copies of every game, one never gets out of the shrink wrap, and you play the other one."

However, there is no indication that Sony will change its mind on this. In July, Sony acknowledged “strong views” from the video game community on the issue, but insisted it wouldn't budge . Elsewhere, the biggest game of the year has no physical version. There are no plans at all for a disc version of GTA 6 , and even the special edition contains a code in an otherwise empty box.

Insomniac’s brutal superhero game was the second best-seller on PS5 last month, beaten only by EA Sports FC 27. EA’s soccer game sold close to 5 million copies on PS5 and 1.65 million on Xbox, reflecting the difference in install base between the two consoles.

How to Fish and Wardogs both outperformed Wolverine when factoring in PC as a platform. Wardogs closed in on 3 million sales, carried by strong word of mouth and viral social media clips of its combat sandbox. Only EA Sports FC 27 on PS5 outsold the Bulkhead and Team 17 shooter in September.

Many other titles were off to a much slower start in September. Ampere’s data shows 305,000 sales on PS5 for Control: Resonant and 291,000 for Silent Hill: Townfall . The Blood of Dawnwalker , the debut RPG from a team of former The Witcher developers at Rebel Wolves, fared much better, boasting 1.8 million sales across all platforms.

articles.title: Dandelion Void - Official Demo Launch Trailer | Triple-i Initiative Fall Showcase 2026 - IGN

articles.title: The Judge Dredd/Biker Mice From Mars Crossover Spawns an Epic Action Figure - NYCC 2026
articles.body:
2026 has been packed full of strange and wonderful comic book crossovers, and perhaps none more strange than Judge Dredd/Biker Mice From Mars. Perhaps it's only fitting that the comic has now inspired an action figure.

As revealed during Nacelle's NYCC panel, the comic is getting a companion figure featuring Biker Mice leader Throttle wearing the iconic Judge Dredd armor. IGN can exclusively debut the first images of this truly epic figure. Check them out in the slideshow gallery below:

Judge Dredd/Biker Mice From Mars Throttle Figure - Image Gallery

This is quite an impressive pair. The Throttle figure features the iconic hero decked out in Dredd's armor. That figure is accompanied by a new vehicle that merges his trademark Martian Monster Bike with Dredd's Lawmaster. The figure includes plenty of other accessories, like an unmasked head and various weapons and interchangeable hands.

“It’s great to work with teams who share our love of both nostalgia and the future, so working with Nacelle and the legendary Biker Mice from Mars is right up our street,” said Jason Kingsley, CBE, co-founder and CEO of Rebellion, in a statement.

“Working with the wonderful folks at Rebellion on this comic and toy crossover has been one of the most delightful experiences in my career,” said Nacelle CEO Brian Volk-Weiss. “We’re excited to give fans an epic crossover event for these two beloved characters”.

Both the Throttle figure and the bike vehicle are available to preorder on the Nacelle website and Rebellion's site .

IGN can also exclusively reveal the solicitation and cover art for Judge Dredd/Biker Mice From Mars #2. Check out the slideshow gallery below:

Judge Dredd/Biker Mice From Mars #2 Cover Art Gallery

Issue, $7.99, 40 Pages, Cardstock Cover, Full Color, Standard Size, Series Finale In Stores January 27

MEGA-CITY MADNESS! The dimension-bending crossover event 22 centuries in the making begins its final countdown as rapid-fire writers Dan Watters (M.A.S.K., Batman: Final Countdown) & Ryan O’Sullivan (Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War) and powerhouse artist Jordi Tarragona (Injustice: Gods Among Us) launch the future’s most feared lawman into a head-to-head showdown against Mars’ mutant bikers . . . and his own twisted reflection.

Lured by the cross-dimensional energy surrounding Throttle, Vinnie, and Modo, Judge Death has returned to Mega-City One, and now the most lethal entity in existence wants to claim every soul in the city! To prevent utter annihilation, Dredd and the Biker Mice must forge an uneasy alliance, but the law and rebellion don’t necessarily mix! With Limburger and Karbunkle looting Mega-City’s tech as reality is rent asunder, every block is about to become an all-out war zone! Can the Biker Mice survive Dredd’s fury as his futuristic metropolis erupts into a maelstrom of mayhem and malice . . . and, even if they do, how will they make it home in one piece?

You can preorder Judge Dredd/Biker Mice From Mars #2 at your local comic shop .

articles.title: Joe Manganiello Reveals Being Cast as Deathstroke in Ben Affleck's Batman Movie Motivated Him to Overcome Near-Fatal Health Crisis
articles.summary: Actor Joe Manganiello has shared a hellish story about how being cast as Deathstroke in Ben Affleck's scrapped Batman movie motivated to overcome drastic health issues.
articles.body:
Actor Joe Manganiello has shared a hellish story about how being cast as Deathstroke in Ben Affleck's scrapped Batman movie motivated him to overcome some drastic health issues.

The Hollywood Reporter has shared an excerpt from Manganiello's new memior, titled Bloodlines, where he shares the nightmare-ish situation he was dealing with when he was cast as Deathstroke. The actor was set to play the villain in a Batman film directed by and starring Ben Affleck in the late 2010s. As it turns out, Manganiello was suffering from a ton of health issues that nearly killed him around the time of his casting.

The actor revealed that he collapsed on the set of a Seal Team Six mini-series in 2016, resulting in an extended hospital stay so doctors could discern the unexplainable autoimmune disease that was "attacking his thyroid and ravaging his intestines." He experienced rectal bleeding that stained his hospital room, and said that his entire large intestine had been turned to "pus" and was about to explode, which would've been fatal. Doctors had to remove much of it and replaced it with an ostomy bag, which holds digestive waste in a pouch that stays on the outside of his body.

During his recovery, the actor went from 235 pounds to 176 pounds and was struggling with the bag, which would leak and erupt waste in the middle of the night. The entire experience took a heavy mental toll on him, leading to nervous breakdowns. However, he was given a glimmer of hope for a return to normalcy and a chance at advancing his career with the biggest role he'd been offered to date.

Ben Affleck offered the actor the opportunity to play Deathstroke, the lead antagonist in a new standalone Batman film. Manganiello's then-wife Sofia Vergara pleaded for him to not take the job due to his fragile physical state. However, he believed this was a strong movitator to overcome his health issues.

"Sofia couldn’t bring herself to congratulate me on landing the biggest role of my career," reads an excerpt. "She’d just watched me die and come back to life through the marvel of modern science, and I think during my illness part of her had begun to adapt to the traumatic thought of living her life without me. Now, here I was, packing to leave her for an unbelievably high-stakes job that I was in no shape to take. Hard as it was for her to understand, I needed it to survive. The role contained the shred of hope that I might get my life back in some capacity, and I had to believe it was possible."

The actor hid his health situation from Affleck and the crew, which was apparently quite difficult when he went to go for a suit fitting. In order to avoid any leakages or accidents from his ostomy bag, Manganiello avoided eating for 18 hours in order to clear out his digestive system and ensure that the bag was completely empty when he went into his fitting. Had he not, the tight spandex and armor plating for his Deathstroke suit may have compressed his bag to the point of exploding.

Ultimately, it sounds like an extremely dreadful experience. Ben Affleck's Batman film was eventually canceled in favor of a reboot with Robert Pattinson and director Matt Reeves. Affleck later revealed that he walked away from the film due to his ongoing struggles with alcoholism and depression around that time. A close friend reportedly told the actor that although the script was good, he would drink himself to death if he'd moved forward on it .

Affleck did release test footage of Manganiello's Deathstroke during the pre-production process, and Manganiello himself has talked loosely about what that role would've looked like. He described the character as being similar to a "horror movie villain" that was attempting to destroy Bruce Wayne's life as revenge for some unmentioned incident.

“It was a really dark story in which Deathstroke was like a shark or a horror movie villain that was dismantling Bruce’s life from the inside out," Manganiello said in 2020 . "It was this systemic thing: He killed everyone close to Bruce and destroyed his life to try and make him suffer because he felt that Bruce was responsible for something that happened to him.”

Joe Manganiello did eventually get to briefly play Deathstroke via two cameos in the theatrical and director's cuts of Justice League. He had hoped to continue playing the role, but it seems unlikely that will ever happen as part of DC's new rebooted universe. In 2021, following his appearance in Zack Snyder's Justice League, the actor stated that he had made his desire to keep playing Deathstroke known to the studio.

"It's not up to me, but I have made it clear that I would do it again. I think everyone knows, because I talked about it, that there was an origin film in the works and there was a treatment that I worked on with the studio for about six months for a Deathstroke origin. All of that story is there, ready to go. Would I do it again? Yeah, I've made it clear that I would, so it's up to the studio. And if that's a priority for them, then yeah, absolutely I would do it."

articles.title: A Live-Action Cyberpunk 2077 Movie Is in the Works at Paramount
articles.summary: Paramount Pictures is developing a live-action Cyberpunk 2077 film.
articles.body:
Paramount Pictures is developing a live-action Cyberpunk 2077 film.

Deadline has reported that the film will be produced by Lorenzo di Bonaventura, who is best known for producing the Transformers and GI Joe films. CD Projekt Red is also onboard to produce, though there is no word on any actors, writers, or directors attached to the project. It's unclear if it will faithfully adapt the titular video game from 2020, or if this will be another story set in the Cyberpunk universe, similar to Netflix's animated Edgerunners series.

If this is a straight up adaptation, Paramount already has some built-in starpower that it can utilize. In the game, Keanu Reeves played Johnny Silverhand, a radical Tyler Durden-style character that lives in the protagonist's head. Idris Elba also joined the game's cast in an expansion known as Phantom Liberty, which feels like a really cool storyline to adapt, though it may not work as well as a mainstream entry point into that universe. Either way, it's exciting to hear that Night City is making its way to the big screen.

CD Projekt Red is also hard at work on the next Cyberpunk game , which is expected to release after The Witcher 4. As a result, we may not see the next game until 2029 or 2030 at the absolute earliest. But that may also be perfect timing, as a Cyberpunk film may not be ready until around that time either. Reeves has already expressed interest in appearing in the next Cyberpunk game , so maybe he'd play Johnny Silverhand on the big screen too.

Paramount is leaning heavy into major video game adaptations, as it has Street Fighter releasing next weekend. In 2028, the studio will also release a Call of Duty movie written by Taylor Sheridan and directed by Peter Berg. Paramount is making all kinds of big moves, as it just merged with Warner Brothers , meaning it has a wealth of new IP to take advantage of.

articles.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation Announces an NPC-ified Version of Shiva Voiced by Marisha Ray | NYCC 2026
articles.summary: The Critical Role performer is also the real-life wife of the voice of Vincent Valentine.
articles.body:
A seemingly new type of Shiva is joining Final Fantasy VII Revelation. At the game’s New York Comic Con panel, it was revealed that Critical Role performer Marisha Ray is joining Revelation as “Polydroid Shiva.” It wasn’t explained how, exactly, this pointy version of the series-recurring ice lady summon will fit into Revelation, but in the BTS clip played during the panel, she seemed to be announcing a snowboarding minigame and blamed Vincent for her “situation.”

“Have you any of the faintest idea of the consternation you’ve caused?” Polydroid Shivia says. “Polydroid problems aren’t my purview,” Vincent replies. (Cold, brother!) She then demands him to, “Drop on a board, caped one, and give my slopes a spin. Let us see how you carve!”

Ray stood up from the front row of the panel, but did not join the stage. Moderator Lucy James asked Matt Mercer, the voice of Vincent Valentine and Ray’s real-life husband and Critical Role co-star, what it was like acting alongside Ray and seeing her in the game. “It was amazing, are you kidding me!” Mercer said. “[Shiva] is her favorite summon in the whole series.”

When they realized they were sharing scenes together after Ray was booked, he said they celebrated, but had one hesitation. “Talking to the team, too, it was like, ‘I hope this wasn’t any nepotism scenario,’” Mercer said. “It was like, ‘Oh no, they didn’t know she was your wife.’ I was like, ‘That’s right, you earned that, baby!’”

The hour-long panel was a sendoff for the cast, many of whom have spent nearly seven years recording for these roles. Cody Christian, who voices Cloud, estimated he’d spent “800 hours collectively” in the booth to nail his lines. “Every inflection, every breath, it all matters. We’d spend 10 minutes on 3 wo r ds just to make sure it was right,” he said.

Final Fantasy VII Revelation releases on April 8, 2027. Director Naoki Hamaguchi (who was not at the NYCC panel, but thanked fans via prerecorded video message) has said that the game will take more than 100 hours for completionists to beat .

Manuel encouraged her to join the family for Pokémon GO raids at the park, giving her a reason to get outside and reconnect. Now three generations play together every day, and Idalise says the game has 'completely transformed' her family.

articles.title: Backrooms on 4K UHD and Blu-ray Is Up for Preorder at Amazon
articles.summary: The psychological horror movie Backrooms is getting a home release in November, when it hits 4K UHD Blu-ray for the first time.
articles.body:
Here’s one for fans of horror movies or liminal spaces in general. Backrooms , the major motion picture based on a concept that originated as an internet creepypasta, is up for preorder on Amazon on 4K UHD and Blu-ray . It's an A24 release, and it comes with six collectible postcards. It will be released on November 17.

Backrooms stars Chiwetel Ejiofor, Renate Reinsve, and Mark Duplass, and not many other people. It’s a spare film that moves slowly yet assuredly through its unsettling narrative. Ejiofor plays a down-on-his-luck furniture store manager who discovers that the basement of the store contains a portal into a strange, seemingly alternate world.

The portal leads to a seemingly endless string of connected yellow rooms and hallways, all lit by fluorescent lights and designed with weird and off-putting architecture. There are nooks and crannies where none should be, and half-walls and items from the outside world placed haphazardly in nonsensical locations. The rooms also seem to be home to a violent creature lurking in the shadows.

I watched it recently when it debuted on HBO , and I can attest it’s an unsettling movie that goes some very strange places. It was directed by Kane Parsons, and based partially on a series of YouTube videos he filmed and uploaded starting in 2022. This movie is Parsons’ directorial debut, and according to Wikipedia , “At age 20, Parsons became the youngest director to have a film debut at number one at both the domestic and global box offices, with Backrooms grossing over $400 million worldwide.”

In IGN’s Backrooms review , critic Lex Briscuso wrote, “Backrooms expertly expands on the conceptual groundwork of the YouTube series with smart visual composition, beautifully terrifying production design, a complex protagonist, and a return to Kane Parsons’ roots of computer generated sequences that pack a serious punch.”

For more, check out our full list of all the biggest upcoming 4K UHD and Blu-ray release dates .
