articles.title: MrBeast Auctions Off the Original Sketch of His Logo With Estimated Value of $20,000
articles.summary: The original pencil sketch of Jimmy ‘MrBeast’ Donaldson’s famous logo is being auctioned off, and experts estimate that it could be worth over $20,000.
articles.body:
The original pencil sketch of Jimmy ‘MrBeast’ Donaldson’s famous logo is being auctioned off, and experts estimate that it could be worth over $20,000.

MrBeast is basically synonymous with YouTube these days, and it’s not hard to see why; he’s the single most-subscribed individual creator on the platform (520 million), famous for his over-the-top challenge videos, eye-popping cash prizes, and massive philanthropic projects.

Fourteen years after starting his channel in 2012, MrBeast is now selling one of the ideas that has made him a household name — the very first pencil sketch of his iconic blue tiger logo.

It adorns every bit of MrBeast’s branding, from his YouTube channel to his merchandise and even his very own chocolate bar line. Of course, this particular sketch doesn’t have any coloring, but shows the tiger (or, here, a leopard or spotted cat of some kind) as we know it today, minus the pink lightning bolt over its eye.

The 8.5-by-11-inch drawing is being put up for bidding as part of Heritage Auctions’ October 23 – 25 Fall Sports Catalog Auction. Experts estimate that, thanks to MrBeast’s mind-blowing net worth and prestige as a content creator, this simple sketch could be worth $20,000 or more.

Reps at Heritage Auctions explained that this logo was created around 2018 during a quick, 10-minute brainstorming session. Speaking with Wired , Donaldson explained how he first came up with the design, admitting that “even though that logo has probably been seen a hundred billion times, I actually put very little thought into it.”

“When I was a little kid I just kind of designed a tiger, and here we are,” he said. “My name, my logo, probably should have had more thought behind it, I’ll admit it.”

He also revealed that even he “doesn’t really know” what type of big cat the animal in his logo is supposed to be. “I guess it’s kind of like a tiger,” he told Wired, though the early concept art being sold at auction suggests that it was initially supposed to be a leopard or panther of some kind.

MrBeast has grown from his roots as a viral YouTuber into a fully-fledged game show host with his own series on Amazon’s Prime Video, Beast Games . It's got two seasons that are available to watch right now, and has been renewed for a third one. He has also co-authored a book with Alex Cross writer James Patterson called The Most Dangerous Games, which, as you can probably guess, follows 100 strangers who enter a contest for the chance of winning a billion dollars.

articles.title: Matchbox The Movie Is Exactly What You Expect From A Movie Tied To Wee Metal Cars That Don't Do Anything Except Roll
articles.summary: Matchbox The Movie is glitzy, glossy and hollow, never even trying to present something original. Everything is safe and familiar and easy, which has always been Hollywood's go-to answer for trying to hit as many quadrants as possible, thus potentially making the most money.
articles.body:
Matchbox The Movie premieres October 9 on Apple TV.

It's hard separating the cars from the cartist here. Matchbox The Movie starts as a ridiculous ad for the 70-year-old toy line, which are literally just small die-cast metal cars, and then cranks up its volume for some empty, fleeting nonsense. Apple TV has a strong case for having the best quality shows of the Streaming Wars but it's not perfect. Like other streamers, it's also given us dumb bullshit. Let's dig deeper...

Sadly, the best thing about Matchbox The Movie -- which is that it goes overboard with large-scale, globe-trotting action -- is hamstrung by it being a watch at home on your couch affair. Look, it's all forgettable, and a waste of a Marvel movie-sized budget, but at least on the big screen the big set pieces from director Sam Hargrave (stunt coordinator for Infinity War and Endgame, director of both Extraction* flicks for Netflix) could get the presentation everyone's hard work deserves. Nothing's ever going to take your breath away on a 55" screen though.

(*Despite them also being non-theatrical releases, y'all should check out the insane Oners in this franchise.)

Matchbox The Movie centers on middle school friends in a small Ohio town, who call themselves the Matchbox Gang (ugh) because they somehow enjoy playing with teensy cars in the year of our lord 1997. Four of them grow up to have careers based on the specific Matchbox vehicle they liked as a kid (you can almost hear the Mattel boardroom execs hubbub positively at this idea). One of the gang, however, Sean, moves away and winds up becoming a no-ties, family-doesn't-exist dickhead secret agent. John Cena plays adult Sean, who returns home after decades and inadvertently gets his estranged pals roped up in a dangerous international conspiracy involving a missing nuke. Now they all must work together to clear their names and save the day.

Jessica Biel, Teyonah Parris, Sam Richardson, and Arturo Castro round out the cast, along with Danai Gurira, and Corey Stoll. None of these folks are to blame here. They're all fun, talented performers more or less wasted in a movie that feels like it came from an episode of The Studio (also available on Apple TV). It just makes you feel bad when these guys do their best to make the movie's meager emotional moments work.

These aren't really characters, though, they're brief character summaries. Construction truck guy never wants to leave town. His flying wife wants to see the world. Paramedic race car woman wants to help people. And quickly. Fun fact: Since race car lady (Biel) is the woman Cena's spy dude has been pining for, she has to be available. But it's been decades so she had to have been married before. I thought to myself, "I bet she says I was married, didn't take ." And guess what, you guys?

Matchbox is glitzy, glossy and hollow, never even trying to present something original. Everything is safe and familiar and easy, which has always been Hollywood's go-to answer for trying to hit as many quadrants as possible, thus potentially making the most money. But it's always, no matter how many times the lesson hasn't been learned, led to unexceptional dust. You also can't trick people into thinking your movie is good by having your characters recurrently reference better action movies.

There's a chance this will be a disposable "streaming hit." Like a Red Notice or a Back in Action or a War Machine. It's a futile accolade, based on metrics with too many loopholes, workarounds, and sleight of hand. It means people will put this on their TV, on a service they already subscribe to. It could be on in the background or it could provide TV light while falling asleep. What it definitely means is that people will easily do that rather than buy a ticket to see it in the theater.

Let's talk about what this is: it's a multi-million dollar mistake based on the worst takeaways from the massive success of the Barbie movie . It was movie studio and toy company heads thinking that Barbie was a hit because it was based on doll people know. There could be no other reason, right, that people, primarily women, went and saw Barbie over and over again? Here now stands the grotesque love child of this obtuse reasoning. There were then pitches all over town for toy movies. What can we do with Matchbox? The answer is, obviously, nothing. Now, I firmly believe that this film was probably the best idea for a Matchbox movie. But the best idea for a Matchbox movie is still a terrible idea for a movie. If something's the best-worst, or the least-awful, don't make it.

Ultimately, any movie based on a toy or a video game or a comic is an ad for that product. Barbie worked because it magically side-stepped that puddle by being about something socially relevant and important. Matchbox was never ever going to be capable of that. Barbie was also damn funny. This movie has laughs you can count on one hand if you're feeling charitable (all, in part, thanks to Sam Richardson). Matchbox The Movie is like when Wayne's World had to shill for Noah's Arcade. There's even a moment in the beginning where a character muses about the history of the Matchbox toy line, like it's Americana we should salute.

articles.title: Xbox XP's First Task Should Be the Halo Movie We Never Got
articles.summary: Microsoft has just announced Xbox XP, a new division aimed at getting cool experiences – be they movies, TV shows, theme park attractions, etc. – made out of its many intellectual properties. And that's how Microsoft can erase the memory of the TV show you probably already forgot anyway. No, I'm not suggesting that they necessarily dust off Garland's 20-year-old script (unless it's awesome, then by all means, do it!), but by turning Halo into the movie we deserve but never got.
articles.body:
Halo should've never ended up as a mid-at-best TV show on Paramount Plus. Instead of " Master Cheeks ," we should've gotten a big-budget big-screen feature film with Xbox's halo-nuking helmeted hero. And that was the plan. Guys dressed up as Master Chief even delivered 28 Days Later scribe Alex Garland's script to various movie studios as Microsoft tried to sell the film to the highest bidder. But things went how they went .

Now, however, Microsoft has just announced Xbox XP , a new division aimed at getting cool experiences – be they movies, TV shows, theme park attractions, etc. – made out of its many intellectual properties. And that's how Microsoft can erase the memory of the TV show you probably already forgot anyway. No, I'm not suggesting that they necessarily dust off Garland's 20-year-old script (unless it's awesome, then by all means, do it!), but by turning Halo into the movie we deserve but never got.

Sure, TV shows are great because they're often cheaper than films and can be stretched out over multiple years, potentially sustaining added interest in the brand longer than a single-pop movie would. But short of making something legendary on the level of Breaking Bad or The Sopranos, the ceiling is a lot lower on a TV show than on a movie, which could make a billion dollars if executed correctly. It's not that Halo can't work as a TV show (despite Paramount Plus's evidence to the contrary), it's just that Halo is a game with the right combination of lore, action, and established cultural cachet that it would be best served as a big-budget movie. And finding the right people to make exactly that should be Xbox XP's first order of business.

Canon doesn't really matter for a movie, because a major motion picture should probably just tell the story of the legendary first game. Not only because it's a great story, but because it's already tailor-made for a three-act movie. We start where the game does, waking up Master Chief from cryosleep aboard the Pillar of Autumn as the Covenant attack. Chief steps out, kicks a bunch of ass, and then there's time to fill in some backstory and do a bit of character intros for Chief, Cortana, and the Spartan program with Dr. Halsey. Then we head down to the Halo ring, mix some Covenant backstory in with more action, and then the non-gamer audience gets surprised with the introduction of The Flood (it'd be important to not give away that twist in the trailers), before things escalate in the third act as Chief and Cortana destroy the whole damn thing.

Look, I'm obviously no scriptwriter, but my point is that the first priority of Xbox XP should be getting Halo on the big screen. The franchise is in a state of metamorphosis as it is, with Activision now taking on responsibility for development of the next mainline game . With a team being spun up and probably plugged into the efficient Call of Duty pipeline pretty soon, my money is on Activision shipping its first big Halo game in four years. It could be three and it probably won't be five, knowing that Sharma wants Halo back in the marketplace, so my money's on four (with three-year development cycles after that, but we can talk about that another time ). My point is: that's plenty of time to get a Halo movie together, and perhaps even launch them together for the Ultimate Corporate Synergy™ that new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma would no doubt love to see.

And fortunately, finding talented people to put a Halo movie together shouldn't be a problem. After all, this is a franchise that, in addition to the aforementioned and accomplished Garland, has also had names like Stephen Spielberg and Peter Jackson attached to it at various points over the years. Halo as a whole is in desperate need of a turnaround, whether it's rebounding from the abandoned two-season Paramount Plus show or bouncing back from an up-and-down couple of decades under the stewardship of 343 Industries/Halo Studios. We'll see what Activision can do on the games side of things, but it's up to Xbox XP to show the world how serious they are about this new division by turning Halo into the blockbuster movie it was always meant to be.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Microsoft’s new Windows Search is exactly what Windows 11 needs
articles.summary: Windows Search is being overhauled with a focus on speed and capability.
articles.body: Windows Search has been one of the most frustrating parts of Windows 11, and now Microsoft is addressing this with a significant overhaul. A new redesigned Windows Search is now in testing that is much faster, more capable, and a lot more modern. “This new Windows Search experience is built for speed,” says Anshul Rawat, corporate vice president of the Windows product team at Microsoft. “It’s built on WinUI 3 and is part of our broader investment in modernizing our core Windows experiences.” Microsoft says early testing of this new search has shown “substantial improvements in performance and memory usage,” meaning the company isn’t adding extra bloat to Windows to improve search, either. The UI has also been greatly improved, with speedy animations and a large preview pane. [Image: The inline previews make Windows Search feel a lot faster. While search is being overhauled visually, behind the scenes Microsoft is also improving the basics. “We’re also improving how Windows Search understands what you’re looking for, including better matching for typos and synonyms,” says Rawat. I got to try out this new Windows Search interface at Microsoft’s Windows and Surface event yesterday, and I was impressed with just how quick it is and how decluttered it feels. Right now if you search for something like the height of an actor it will take a few seconds to figure it out and show you essentially a miniature Bing result. The new Windows Search just surfaces the result inline, much like the modern search interfaces you see in iOS and Android. These inline results also extend to previews of PowerPoint presentations, photos, and other files. [Image: You’ll be able to use search to send text messages. The most impressive part of this new Windows Search is being able to use it like a launcher, just like many third-party tools, and have it take actions for tasks like turning Bluetooth or dark mode on and off. You can even ask search to minimize windows, or open apps side-by-side. If you use Phone Link, these actions will also extend to your phone so you could simply type “text mom, I’m running late” and it will send a text message from your phone. Microsoft is testing this new Windows Search interface with its Windows Insiders right now, so that should mean we’ll see it appear in Windows 11 in the coming months. “Looking to next year, work is already underway to bring the new Windows Search experience to the Start menu and have it adapt naturally to different taskbar positions and Windows configurations,” says Rawat. “Our goal is to make Windows Search more capable, with more natural ways to express what you need, richer information in context, and more ways to get things done directly from search.”

articles.title: Jessica Chastain Reveals the ‘Painful’ Secret to her Terrifying Smile in Other Mommy
articles.summary: Jessica Chastain explained how she pulled off the terrifying facial expression she makes as the Other Mommy, saying that physical “pain” was a central part of getting her uncanny smile just right.
articles.body:
Jessica Chastain explained how she pulled off the terrifying facial expression she makes in the Other Mommy, saying that physical “pain” was a central part of getting her uncanny smile just right.

Chastain stars in Universal Pictures’ Other Mommy , where she plays both the mother of a young girl and the entity that haunts her family. It’s a Coraline-style premise that adds another horror film to her steadily-growing roster of projects in the genre ( IT Chapter 2 , Mama, Crimson Peak ).

The big draw for this film is Chastain’s horrifying transformation from a caring mother to a bloodthirsty entity wearing her skin. Trailers for the movie show the acclaimed actress in both roles; when she plays the entity, she wears a dead-eyed expression with a wide, almost painful-looking smile.

It turns out that this smile does, indeed, channel some element of physical pain, as told by Chastain during an appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live where she explained how she came up with the entity’s distinct facial expression.

“I thought about this entity holding on the skin of a person, and maybe that’s the painful thing, like maybe you’re holding a box for a long time that’s very heavy. So the tension in your body, you have to hold this, and then, you have to smile, because you need a child to think you’re safe and approachable,” she said.

She then demonstrated the smile for the audience and even shed a tear right on cue. It was an impressive display of her acting ability, which Kimmel pointed out once her demo was done.

“I am a trained actress,” she joked. “You know what it is? I really felt the pain in my body, and that’s why, sometimes, you can see in the neck in the pictures — but then try to be as nice as possible. Don’t show your teeth.”

Thus far, early reviews for Other Mommy have been rather merciless ; viewers who’ve seen it ahead of its October 9 theatrical release have called it “more silly than it is scary,” “truly dreadful,” and “masterfully cringe” on social media.

Viewers will have to judge for themselves when the film comes out tomorrow. For now, we can hope that Chastain’s impressive acting carries Other Mommy. That smile is certainly unsettling all on its own!

articles.title: Did Yankees bro curse the Bronx Bombers?
articles.summary: The New York Yankees haven’t won a title since Yankees bro went viral in the 2010 ALCS
articles.body:
For me, one of the most memorable moments from the 2010 Texas Rangers playoff run — the season the Rangers won a playoff series for the first time ever, the season the Rangers went to the World Series for the first time ever — is a scene from a play where things went bad for the Rangers.

Specifically, it involves the second inning of Game Four of the ALCS, when the New York Yankees, down 2 games to 1, took the lead in a game that they needed to win to bring the series back to even.

The first ten batters of the game had been retired — six Rangers hitters sat down by Yankee starter A.J. Burnett, four Yankees hitters by Tommy Hunter of the Rangers. The #5 hitter for the Yanks, Robinson Cano, got down 0-1 to Hunter before lofting a fly ball to the wall in right field. Nelson Cruz looked like he might have a play on it, but it was caught by a backwards hat wearing Yankees bro in the first row.

The immediate aftermath of the play was captured in this immortal gif:

I have no idea how many times in my life I've watched this. Hundreds? Thousands? I feel like I have watched it at least 50 times just today, thinking about doing this post, and then with it cycling on the screen as I continue typing this post.

I really get so much joy from this gif. I feel like Sam Malone on Cheers with the painting of the dogs playing poker, talking about how he sees something new every time he looks at it. There's so much going on there, and I wish I could find the old SBN piece — I think by Jon Bois, but maybe by Grant Brisbee or Jeff Sullivan — where he offers up a backstory for each person in the gif, and read it again, and make all of y'all read it again.

Part of the reason that I can get joy from this gif is that, well, the Rangers went on to win the game, and then the series. Kind of like I'd probably find some humor and lightness in another extra base hit over Nelson Cruz's head that occurred a little over a year later, had the Rangers ended up winning that Game 6 (or the subsequent Game 7).

But at the time, it sucked, and I hated the Yankee bro, and everyone else in this shot — yes, including the popcorn guy in glasses, and the two different kids — with a degree of sports hate that I had previously reserved solely for Dwight Clark and for the 1996 Seattle Mariners.

The hate didn't last long. The Rangers tied it up in the top of the third, gave up singletons in the third and fourth to go down 3-2, but then exploded for eight runs in the final four innings,* rolling to an easy 10-3 win.

* The Rangers scored five runs in all off of Burnett, the final three coming on a two out, three run home run by Bengie Molina in the top of the sixth, a play that may have inspired my "most momentum-shifting play in baseball" mantra. They scored one off of Boone Logan, one off of Joba Chamberlain, and three off of Sergio Mitre. The only Yankee pitcher who made an appearance and didn't give up a run was future Rangers great David Robertson.

Texas was up 3-1 in the series, and though they fell to the Yankees in Game 5 behind a bad C.J. Wilson start and an offense that managed just two runs on 13 hits (one of which was a Matt Treanor home run, shoutout to Mr. May! ), they rolled over New York in their return to Arlington for the Good Game 6. Colby Lewis — who was incredible in that postseason run — threw eight innings of three hit, one run ball, Vlad Guerrero and Nelson Cruz sparked a four run fifth to give the Rangers a comfy lead, and Neftali Feliz finished it off by freezing ARod on a called strike three:

Seriously, watch this clip again (even though you have to sit through a stupid 15 second commercial because MLB.com has to monetize their video snippets). Remember that feeling? Remember how amazing that was? I still get goosebumps when I watch the Corey Seager World Series home run, and I still get goosebumps when I watch this.

So, yeah, the Yankees bro gif is fun to me. It makes the Rangers comeback, and ultimate series win over New York, all the more delightful.

That said, in the aftermath of last night's Yankees game-tying homer that wasn't, I was thinking about the Yankees bro clip, and the timing of it in relation to the Yankees' recent history.

The 2010 Yankees, you may recall, were the defending World Series champions, having beaten the Philadelphia Phillies in the 2009 World Series four games to two. (Both losses, incidentally, were against Cliff Lee, who shut out the Yankees on two hits over eight innings in Game 3 of the 2010 ALCS. The Yankees, of course, tried to get Lee from the Mariners at the 2010 trade deadline before the Rangers out-bid them, and there was talk that Lee was in the Yankees' head, much like Mike Scott was in the head of the Yankees' crosstown rivals in the NLCS in 1986).

The 2010 Yankees were favored over the Rangers, even though the Rangers had homefield advantage. The Yankees had the second best record in the A.L., with 95 wins, while the Rangers had the worst record of the four A.L. playoff teams, at "just" 90-72. The Yankees still had Derek Jeter and Jorge Posada and Mariano Rivera and Andy Pettitte from their dynasty teams, plus high-priced former Rangers Mark Teixeira and Alex Rodriguez, stud second baseman Robinson Cano (who the Rangers could have had in the ARod trade, though they picked Joaquin Arias instead) in his prime, C.C. Sabathia fronting the rotation…

And the Rangers…well, they were the Rangers. Yes, they traded for Cliff Lee, and signed an aging Vlad Guerrero to be their DH. But otherwise, they were relying on a bunch of hitters without playoff experience, as well a converted reliever and a guy who got run out of the majors and had to go to Japan in the rotation behind Lee. The end of the 90s saw the Rangers chased from the playoffs by a Yankees dynasty, and the start of the 2010s seemed to be setting the stage for the same thing to happen in a new decade.

Texas ceded homefield advantage one game into the series, blowing a 5-0 lead that included a gruesome five run eighth inning where five pitchers — C.J. Wilson, Darren Oliver, Darren O'Day, Clay Rapada and Derek Holland — combined to retire none of the first seven batters in the inning. The Rangers won big in Games 2 and 3, but when Cano homered off of Big Game Hunter to give the Yankees a 1-0 lead in Game 4, when backwards hat Yankees douche was yelling and posturing and Horatio Sanz's twin was cheering and the Sopranos extra in the 72 inch waist jeans was yelling "Fuck you! Fuck you! Fuck you!" over and over, it felt like an ill harbinger, a bad omen, the beginning of the end of the Rangers' magical run.

In another timeline, maybe that's the case. In another timeline, the Burnett stifles the Rangers in this Game 4, and Wilson's Game 5 egg is followed up by a slightly less effective Colby Lewis in Game 6, with Philip Hughes avoiding the crooked number in the bottom of the fifth in Arlington and David Robertson and Kerry Wood keeping Texas off the board until Mariano Rivera gets Josh Hamilton swinging with two outs in the bottom of the ninth, Rangers fans watching the Yankees celebrate at TBiA before stomping the San Francisco Giants in the World Series.

We aren't in that timeline, though. In this timeline, the Rangers ended the Yankees' hope of repeating as champions, of bringing back the Yankees Dynasty. They rebounded from the Cano home run that set off the iconic celebration in the stands, won the game, and won the series.

The Yankees are still chasing their next ring. When Robinson Cano hit that home run, Yankees fans felt another title was imminent, and even if, somehow, someway, they didn't win it all in 2010, it would just be a brief delay of the inevitable, and the next ring would come in 2011 or 2012, with the Yankees surely having accumulated multiple rings by the time the 2026 season ended.

But that hasn't happened. The Rangers have won more titles since then than the Yankees have. The Rangers have been to three World Series — including 2010 — to the Yankees' one. Nevermind a Yankees dynasty…New York has found it difficult to get past the divisional round during that time.

Could it be that the Yankee bro's celebration, caught on camera, along with the fans around him, caught the eye of the fickle gods of baseball? Could it be that the ostentatiousness and brashness of an entitled fanbase, encapsulated in that that shot, caught the attention of the baseball gods, who decided to punish Yankees fans for their hubris?

Despite consistently running one of the highest payrolls in the game, despite being one of the marquee franchises in the game, the Yankees haven't won a World Series title since. They have now gone 17 seasons without a title, tied for the longest stretch in franchise history since the team won its first title in 1923. Given their payroll, their on-field success in the regular season during that time, you'd have thought they'd have won the World Series at least once in that stretch, right?

Could it be…the Curse of the Yankees Bro?

articles.title: Yankees Star Calls Out Fans For Booing Team Following Loss
articles.summary: Jazz Chisholm Jr. may have played his final game in a New York Yankees uniform, and if Wednesday night’s season-ending loss to the Tampa Bay Rays was his far...
articles.body:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. may have played his final game in a New York Yankees uniform, and if Wednesday night's season-ending loss to the Tampa Bay Rays was his farewell, it certainly wasn't the ending he envisioned.

The Yankees second baseman found himself on the bench for Game 3 of the American League Division Series after manager Aaron Boone chose a different lineup for a must-win contest. When Chisholm finally entered the game as a seventh-inning pinch hitter, the Yankee Stadium crowd's reception was anything but welcoming.

Chisholm popped out to first base while batting for Jose Caballero, prompting loud boos from frustrated fans . The Yankees eventually fell 4-3, completing a three-game sweep that brought their postseason run to an abrupt end.

Chisholm Questions Yankees Fans After Hearing Boos

Afterward, Chisholm questioned why fans would turn against one of their own players during such an important game.

"It's just confusing because it's the playoffs and we're trying to win games," Chisholm told reporters . "So, you're booing a guy that's playing currently, trying to help the team win. And I'm hearing boos instead of trying to hype guys up, you know what I mean?"

Chisholm insisted the reaction didn't bother him personally, pointing out that even Aaron Judge, the team's biggest star, has endured similar treatment from the Bronx crowd.

"It didn't hurt me. Because, as I said, I've seen Aaron Judge get booed here, too. Who am I? That's a three-time MVP," Chisholm added.

Judge, however, offered a different perspective when he faced postseason boos in October 2022. At the time, the Yankees captain acknowledged his struggles and admitted he "would've booed too," explaining that he didn't take the criticism personally.

Chisholm's situation comes with another complication. His defensive mistake in Game 2 had already drawn criticism from fans, and Boone's decision to bench him for the start of Game 3 only added to questions about his standing with the organization.

Chisholm Wants to Stay Despite Growing Free Agency Speculation

Those questions extend well beyond the disappointing playoff exit.

Chisholm is approaching free agency, and there is growing speculation that the Yankees will pursue a different option at second base. Baseball America's Josh Norris and J.J. Cooper have identified the position as an area New York could address during the offseason. At the same time, NJ Advance Media's Randy Miller reported that Chisholm will probably move on.

Despite the uncertainty and hostile reception from fans, Chisholm made it clear that leaving New York isn't his preferred outcome.
